title: Practical Application
description: Helvant doesn't send you to villagers to be seen doing good - he sends you because word is the only reputation a solitary wizard has, and it travels faster than he does anymore. Harbormaster Harmon Voss hasn't had a working beacon in a week and two boats have already turned back from the rocks rather than risk the dark. Ysolt Bracken in Thornfield has been hauling creek water since her well turned foul. A carter named Denner Cobb has sat three days at the Crossroads with a fallen tree across the road and a load of fish going bad in the sun. And there are bandits working that same stretch who won't ask twice before they take something.

objectives.description: Light Harmon Voss's harbor beacon before another boat turns back
objectives.notes: Beacon for guiding ships - player uses fire spell to light it

objectives.description: Purify Ysolt Bracken's well - she's been hauling creek water for a week
objectives.notes: Well has been tainted - requires arcane purification ritual

objectives.description: Clear the tree off the road before Denner Cobb's fish finish spoiling
objectives.notes: Large tree blocks the road - telekinesis or earth magic needed

objectives.description: Drive off the bandits working the travelers on that road
objectives.notes: Combat test - must use magic against real threats

objectives.description: Tell Helvant how the villagers actually took it

notes: Names invented for this pass, no bible basis - local colour: Harmon Voss (Dalhurst harbormaster), Ysolt Bracken (Thornfield well-owner), Denner Cobb (Crossroads carter). Threat: a dark harbor turning ships back, a fouled well, a blocked road with spoiling cargo, bandits working travelers. Giver motive: Helvant's standing in these villages is built favor by favor, with no institution to fall back on if it sours. Consequence: Denner Cobb is written ungrateful even after help - a carter with three days of lost trade behind him already resents needing a stranger's magic to fix it, and says so. Third quest in the chain.
